No, almost certainly not. With six people, microservices mostly add cost: distributed debugging, network failure modes, versioned APIs between services, per-service deploy pipelines, and data consistency problems. The main benefit, letting large teams deploy independently, doesn't apply when everyone fits in one room. Those costs would come straight out of your product velocity.

The case for splitting is narrow. It holds if one component has sharply different scaling or runtime needs (say, ML inference or video processing), if a hard compliance boundary requires isolating certain data, or if the monolith's build and test times are crippling you and modularization hasn't helped. Even then, extract that one piece rather than rewriting everything.

What to do instead if the monolith is painful: enforce module boundaries inside it (Rails engines, Packwerk), speed up CI, and move heavy work into background jobs. This gets you most of the structural benefit and keeps the option to extract a service later.

I don't know what's driving your question. If there's a specific problem, such as slow deploys, scaling limits, or a hiring plan that will triple the team, tell me and I can say whether it changes the answer.
